title: Stock Market Highlights, Jul 29: Sensex rises 888 pts to close at 77,654, Nifty ends at 24,250; Hindustan Unilever, Infosys top gainers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rebounded sharply and ended over 1 per cent higher on Wednesday, led by IT stocks, HDFC Bank and fresh foreign fund inflows.

The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 888.68 points, or 1.16 per cent, to settle at 77,654.60. During the day, it surged 999.57 points, or 1.30 per cent, to 77,765.49.

The 50-share NSE Nifty climbed 264.85 points, or 1.10 per cent, to end at 24,250.20.

From the Sensex pack, Hindustan Unilever surged 4.70 per cent and Infosys jumped 4.50 per cent.

Trent, Larsen & Toubro, Tata Steel, Bharti Airtel, Tata Consultancy Services, HCL Tech and HDFC Bank were also among the gainers.

Adani Ports, Mahindra & Mahindra, Power Grid, Bharat Electronics and NTPC were the laggards.

MAS Financial Services, specialized in MSME financing, announced today its unaudited financial results for Q1 FY27

On a consolidated basis, MAS Financial Services Limited reported Assets Under Management (AUM) of ₹16,122.75 crore and Profit After Tax (PAT) of ₹110.15 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up from ₹13,298.50 crore and ₹86.59 crore, respectively, for the quarter ended June 30, 2025

Nifty Rollover Analysis: Nifty July series transition witnessed the benchmark index securing a 71.8% figure, trailing the prior expiry’s 80.3%. This metric falls short of both three-month (73.9%) and six-month (73.1%) historical averages, hinting at cautious positioning and mildly subdued momentum.

Bank Nifty Rollover Analysis: The banking gauge recorded a 76.3% transition rate, marginally below the preceding month’s 77.2%. By lagging its quarterly (77.0%) and half-yearly (77.1%) benchmarks, this data suggests a slightly defensive sentiment, though underlying resilience remains intact among financial market participants.

Market-Wide Rollover Trends: Broad market changeover climbed to 94.24%, eclipsing the previous expiry’s 93.56% on a comparable day. Surpassing both the 94.2% quarterly and 93.7% semiannual milestones underscores robust cumulative interest, highlighting an overarching optimistic market breadth and sustained institutional engagement.

Nifty Futures Open Interest: August futures-initiated trading holding 145.3 lakh shares, dropping from the preceding cycle’s 194.5 lakh contracts. This notable 49.1 lakh unwinding, paired with a minor 0.5% valuation uptick, implies lightened speculative burdens alongside underlying positive bias, fostering healthier price action.

Bank Nifty Futures Open Interest: Financial index futures commenced August containing 23.3 lakh active contracts, declining from 23.5 lakh previously. This marginal 0.3 lakh contraction, combined with a 1.4% valuation haircut, reveals minor long liquidation, reflecting momentary caution rather than outright structural bearishness.

Rollover Cost: Carrying expenses for Nifty settled at 0.52%, stepping down from the prior period’s 0.62%. This contraction in carrying premiums reflects reduced aggression among bulls, yet indicates sufficient liquidity and a balanced consensus regarding near-term directional trajectories. Banking sector roll cost contracted sharply to 0.49%, heavily discounted against the antecedent 0.80% mark highlighting diminished speculative froth and cautious leveraging, presenting a stabilized footing for potential upcoming upside movements.

Stocks with Increased Interest: INDIGO, JUBLFOOD, BHEL, ALKEM, and INDUSTOWER experienced elevated rollover versus their prior comparable cycles. This amplified carry-forward behavior signifies growing trader conviction and accumulation within these specific equities, potentially foreshadowing continued upward momentum or intense price action.

Stocks with Decreased Interest: SONACOMS, PAGEIND, KFINTECH, PERSISTENT, and ABB registered diminished contract transitions sequentially. The dampened participation reflects waning immediate interest or position unwinding, pointing toward consolidation phases or profit-taking within these corporate counters before new directional bets emerge.

Sectoral Rollover: Telecom, Infrastructure, and Chemicals industries absorbed heightened carry-forward activity, denoting robust sectoral accumulation and optimistic capital rotation. Conversely, Automobile, Textile, and New_Age segments suffered transition drops, implying transient profit-booking or rotational weakness among these distinct economic pockets.

* Consolidated: Net Sales at ₹ 10,521.4 crore (+17.9%); PBDIT margin of 20.6% (+240 bps)

* Standalone: Net Sales at ₹ 9,156.5 crore (+16.7%); PBDIT margin of 22.0% (+259 bps)

* Decorative Business (India) delivered volume and value growth of 9.0% and 16.6% respectively

* Industrial Coatings sustained mid-teen growth momentum complementing the performance of the Decorative segment and driving broad-based growth across the coatings portfolio

* Net Sales for International Business grew by 27.2% in INR terms (20.3% in constant currency), with PBT margin expansion of 275 bps
